# Error-Handling Checklist: Final-PR Template Set — Slice 1, the PR Write-up Artifact

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements covering this artifact's failure,
empty, degraded, and concurrent paths are complete, unambiguous, and consistent
with the binding export-payload contract
**Created**: 2026-08-12
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)
**Contract under check**: [export-payload-contract.md](../contracts/export-payload-contract.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command. It
tests the requirements, not the implementation. Every item asks whether
something is *written down*, never whether code behaves.

**Depth**: standard. **Audience**: reviewer at pull-request time. **Focus
clusters**: the clipboard failure path, and degraded/empty state.

## Requirement Completeness — the clipboard failure path

- [ ] CHK001 Are requirements defined for revealing the exported text in a
      selectable field when clipboard access fails or is refused? [Completeness,
      Spec §FR-028]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the requirement that the artifact must **not** report success on
      a failed copy stated normatively rather than only in an acceptance
      scenario? [Completeness, Spec §FR-028]
- [x] CHK003 Does the spec require that the revealed field be **focusable and
      not disabled**, and that focus move to it? **Resolved** — FR-028 now
      enumerates all four contract steps and states step 2 in full.
      [Resolved, Spec §FR-028]
- [x] CHK004 Does the spec require the revealed field to carry an accessible
      name? **Resolved** — folded into FR-028 step 2, with the reason that focus
      arriving at an unnamed control strands a reader who cannot see the reveal.
      [Resolved, Spec §FR-028]
- [x] CHK005 Does the spec forbid a **second copy attempt** after the first
      fails? **Resolved** — FR-028a carries the prohibition and its reason: the
      attempt's result is ambiguous, and reporting an uncertain success is
      exactly what the contract forbids. [Resolved, Spec §FR-028a]
- [x] CHK006 Does the spec require **exactly one** failure message covering
      every failure mode? **Resolved** — FR-029b requires it and states why
      byte-identity alone did not secure it. [Resolved, Spec §FR-029b]
- [x] CHK007 Is the **reason** the message asserts no cause recorded as a
      requirement? **Resolved** — FR-029b records all four indistinguishable
      modes and the conclusion that naming one would be a guess presented as a
      diagnosis. [Resolved, Spec §FR-029b]
- [x] CHK008 Are requirements defined for the state of the fallback field on a
      **later successful** export? **Resolved** — FR-028a requires every
      invocation to re-hide the field before it attempts its copy, and names the
      sequential case as distinct from FR-026a's concurrent one.
      [Resolved, Spec §FR-028a]
- [x] CHK009 Does any requirement scope **console silence** to the export
      failure path? **Resolved** — FR-028a extends it there and names the
      mechanism: the rejection is handled rather than left to surface as an
      unhandled rejection. [Resolved, Spec §FR-028a]

## Requirement Completeness — the feedback surface

- [x] CHK010 Does the spec require a **single** status region, present from
      load, that sits **outside every fill region**? **Resolved** — FR-027 now
      fixes count, presence from load, and placement, and states that placement
      is the requirement rather than a preference. [Resolved, Spec §FR-027]
- [ ] CHK011 Are the requirements clear that a copy outcome is reported in text
      rather than by colour or animation alone? [Completeness, Spec §FR-027,
      §FR-032]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the success message required to name what the produced text
      actually carries, so it cannot imply a conclusion the text does not
      contain? [Completeness, Contract §Feedback]

## Requirement Clarity — wording constraints that are test-bearing

- [x] CHK013 Does the spec state the **scheme-naming rule** — that feedback text
      says "opened from a filesystem" rather than naming the local-file scheme?

- [ ] CHK014 Is it unambiguous that the `markdown` export kind names its
      **destination, not its encoding**, so neither kind emits markdown syntax?
      [Clarity, Spec §FR-023a]
- [ ] CHK015 Are the four export literals a reviewer must diff — two lead lines,
      two empty-state bodies — pinned as exact strings rather than paraphrased?
      [Clarity, Spec §FR-029a, Contract §Empty-state bodies]

## Scenario Coverage — the empty export

- [ ] CHK016 Are requirements defined for an export invoked with **no question
      written**, requiring the artifact to say so in text rather than emit an
      empty or invented document? [Coverage, Spec §FR-029]
- [ ] CHK017 Is it specified that the empty export still carries the header
      lines naming the artifact and the feature, so it is not a bare sentence?
      [Coverage, Contract §Empty-state bodies]
- [ ] CHK018 Is the requirement that the empty export **deny being an approval**
      stated with its reason — that the realistic misreading of an empty export
      pasted into a pull-request comment is a sign-off? [Clarity, Contract
      §Empty-state bodies]
- [ ] CHK019 Is precedence specified when a reader exports **nothing** and the
      clipboard **also** fails? The contract's feedback table resolves it with
      an "any failure" row that outranks the empty-state row. [Coverage,
      Contract §Feedback]
- [ ] CHK020 Are requirements defined for a section the reader skipped —
      contributing no line, no placeholder, and no count? [Coverage, Spec
      §FR-023, Edge Cases]

## Scenario Coverage — degraded environment

- [ ] CHK021 Are requirements defined for the artifact with the **network
      unavailable**, holding content fully readable and every control operable
      with typeface substitution the only visible difference? [Coverage, Spec
      §FR-004, §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK022 Is the set of external references bounded tightly enough that
      offline behaviour is derivable rather than asserted? [Consistency, Spec

- [ ] CHK023 Are requirements defined for **storage refused** over the local-file
      scheme — the theme control keeps working for the session and reports no
      error, so persistence degrades and never the control? [Coverage, Spec

- [ ] CHK024 Is it clear that the artifact reads only the resolved theme
      attribute and never stored theme state, so a refused read has no path into

## Scenario Coverage — concurrency

- [ ] CHK025 Are requirements defined for **two exports invoked before the first
      settles**, requiring the later invocation's outcome only? [Coverage, Spec
      §FR-026a]
- [ ] CHK026 Is the guard's scope stated precisely — that **both** settle paths
      carry it, not only the rejection path, because a slow success resolving
      after a fast failure is the mirror case? [Clarity, Spec §FR-026a]
- [ ] CHK027 Are the three effects a superseded settle must not have enumerated
      — changes no status text, reveals no fallback text, moves no focus?
      [Completeness, Spec §FR-026a]
- [ ] CHK028 Are the paths that stay **unguarded** named, with the requirement
      that the artifact say why they are safe by construction? [Completeness,
      Spec §FR-026a]
- [ ] CHK029 Does the spec state that this defect is live in all three shipped
      export-carrying templates and MUST NOT be reproduced, so a reviewer reads
      the departure as the fix rather than as the deviation? [Consistency, Spec
      §FR-026a, Plan §Complexity Tracking]

## Edge Case Coverage — the implementation-notes record

- [ ] CHK030 Are **three distinct empty states** required — every task reported
      nothing, no task recorded an entry, the record was unavailable — rather
      than one undifferentiated empty case? [Coverage, Spec §FR-019b]
- [ ] CHK031 Is it specified that the empty state is carried by the **fill**
      rather than by shipped markup, with the reason stated: nothing in the
      artifact reads the record at render time, so the template cannot
      distinguish the cases and the authoring agent can? [Clarity, Spec
      §FR-019b]
- [ ] CHK032 Are all three states justified as **real rather than hypothetical**,
      so a reader cannot dismiss one as defensive? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019b]
- [ ] CHK033 Are requirements defined for a **retry pair** — two entries under
      one task identifier both rendering, in append order, ungrouped and without
      a derived ordinal? [Coverage, Spec §FR-019, §FR-019c]
- [ ] CHK034 Is the standing intro that distinguishes an empty region from a
      broken one required to sit **outside** the marker pair, so it survives
      every fill? [Coverage, Spec §FR-019a]

## Remediation record

Nine gaps were found and all nine are closed in `spec.md`. **Every fix costs
zero authored lines against the 750/800 reviewability budget**, so the 50 lines
of headroom are untouched. Each is either a behaviour the shipped precedent
already implements inside the measured baseline, or a prohibition that forbids
lines rather than requiring them.

| Gap | Closed by | Line cost | Why zero |
|---|---|---|---|
| CHK003 focus moves to a field that is focusable and not disabled | FR-028 step 2 | 0 | The precedent already focuses the field on a delay and ships it with neither `disabled` nor `readonly`; those lines sit inside the C3 288 baseline. |
| CHK004 the field carries an accessible name | FR-028 step 2 | 0 | The precedent already ships a `<label for>` and its rule; the markup sits inside C4's 215 and the rule inside C2's 97, which was measured off those very selectors. |
| CHK005 no second copy attempt | FR-028a | 0 | A prohibition. Forbidding a retry removes lines rather than adding them. |
| CHK006 exactly one failure message | FR-029b | 0 | A cardinality constraint. It forbids additional messages. |
| CHK007 the message asserts no cause, with the reason | FR-029b | 0 | The reason is spec prose. The artifact's own source comment recording it is the precedent's, already counted in the 293 that C3's 288 derives from. |
| CHK008 the fallback re-hides before every attempt | FR-028a | 0 | The precedent's routine already opens by hiding the fallback; those lines are in the C3 baseline. |
| CHK009 the failure path leaves the console silent | FR-028a | 0 | Satisfied by the precedent's two-argument settle plus its `try`/`catch`, both already in the C3 baseline. No new handler. |
| CHK010 one status region, from load, outside every fill region | FR-027 | 0 | The region must exist to satisfy FR-027 either way. This fixes only where it sits, which is a position rather than a line. |
| CHK013 no script literal names the local-file scheme | FR-029c | 0 | A wording constraint. The same string slot carries either form. |

**Net budget effect: 0 lines. Declared total stays 750 against the 800 block.**

Two consistency items resolved as a side effect: CHK035 (the contract's step 2
traced to no requirement) and CHK036 (the acceptance runbook asserted a focus
move no requirement stated). Neither needed a runbook edit.

`data-model.md`'s traceability row was widened from `FR-021 – FR-029` to
`FR-021 – FR-029c, less FR-029a` so the three new requirements map to the script
region rather than falling outside the table.
